name: Nuni, Basinyari dialect
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Kurrle, Gertrud. 1988. Some word tone patterns in Nuni. Journal of West African Languages 18(1): 29-40.
catalog_quote: This paper investigates the possible tone patterns on verbs, nouns and compound nouns in Nuni (Basinyari dialect). Previous work on Nuni tones has been done by Flik (1979) who established the existence of three contrastive tones and Yago (1984) who described the tone system and established tone patterns on simple nouns and verbs. There are three contrastive tones in Nuni, H (high), M (mid), and L (low), represented here by an acute accent, unmarked, and a grave accent respectively. The three tones contrast on one syllable verbs in frames like the following: ... The same tones contrast on two syllable nouns in frames like the following: ... H and M downdrift after L tones in the usual way.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nuni (Basinyari dialect) is described as a three-level tone language (H, M, L contrast lexically on verbs and nouns, with downdrift); the article says nothing about word stress or accent, so no stress-placement rule can be extracted from any source opened.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; dialect differences (Léo vs Basinyari) concern tone patterns and vowel length only.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on words in frame sentences; no word- or phrase-level stress discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Kurrle 1988 describes the Basinyari dialect of (Southern) Nuni, fieldwork based in Léo, with notes on Léo-dialect differences — squarely sout2795. Caution for the list of works to obtain: Prost 1971/1999 'nuni de Pouni' is tagged [nnw] in Glottolog's 1971 record, but Malgoubri 2011 (per Glottolog language code) classes Pouni as 'Yatini du Nord = Northern Nuni [nuv]' (nort2784); Nébié's works (1980 'Le ton en nuni', 1982 thesis, 1985 grammar) concern Northern Nuni per Berthelette 2002:12.

tone_statements.citation: Malgoubri, Pierre. 2011. Recherches dialectologiques et dialectométriques nuni (une langue gurunsi du Burkina Faso). PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden (LUCL). 350 pp.
tone_statements.quote: En n√nì, en plus des consonnes et des voyelles qui sont utilisées pour distinguer des mots, la hauteur de la voix est employée à des fins distinctives. Cette variation de la hauteur de la voix permet d’opposer deux (2) mots dont les signifiants sont par ailleurs identiques. Il y a trois tons phonologiques dans la langue: - un ton haut [ ⁄] - un ton bas [ Ÿ] - un ton moyen [ ¤] … di⁄ « manger » diŸ « monter » di¤ « terrasser » … Dans tous les dialectes n√nì, nous trouvons la présence de ces trois différents tons. … Les différences tonales n’ont pas été examinées et décrites.
tone_statements.translation: In Nuni, besides the consonants and vowels that are used to distinguish words, voice pitch is used for distinctive purposes. This variation in pitch makes it possible to oppose two words whose forms are otherwise identical. There are three phonological tones in the language: a high tone, a low tone, a mid tone … di 'eat', di 'climb', di 'knock down' … In all Nuni dialects we find these three different tones. … The tonal differences have not been examined and described.
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones, high, low and mid, distinguish otherwise identical words (minimal triplets on di, kara); stated to hold for all Nuni dialects incl. Basinyari; tonal dialect differences not studied.
